_comment: Lying where it fell. Said of trees, half of each it is said of lie fallen beside their stumps, each of its own trunk
-- `fallen trees` every tree the Age grows, `fallen oak` and `fallen birch` the one kind wherever it stands; said
alone, every tree. Said of standing stone (`fallen obelisks`, `fallen megaliths`), each stone taller than it is deep
lies knocked over beside its stump. `fallen stars` are meteors, and `fallen leaves` lie thick on any grass.
